scope.focus: Linear algebra from first representations of vectors and equations through abstract finite-dimensional theory, numerical linear algebra, matrix analysis, modern large-scale methods, and research literacy.
includes: Vectors, matrices, systems, linear maps, spaces, bases, dimension, rank, determinants, eigenstructure and inner products
Orthogonality, least squares, spectral theory, SVD, canonical forms, duality, multilinear and tensor structure
Conditioning, floating-point error, numerical stability and matrix factorizations
Sparse and iterative methods, Krylov subspaces, eigenvalue algorithms, graph/spectral methods and matrix functions
Randomized, streaming, mixed-precision, communication-aware and matrix-free linear algebra
Matrix analysis, tensor decompositions, reproducible numerical experiments and research frontiers
delegates: General calculus and real/complex analysis are not silently assumed; when needed they must be bridged or linked to an appropriate mathematics track.
Programming-language mechanics belong to their language tracks; Linear Algebra may use pseudocode or minimal code only to expose mathematics.
Machine-learning-specific modeling belongs to the LLM/ML-related tracks; Linear Algebra owns the mathematical structures those tracks reuse.
